minutes.headline: New APDC member urged a bylaw review; board will not reconsider its Ritter window denial.
minutes.summary: The meeting was mostly a long discussion with new member Nathan Lockwood about the origin and intent of the architectural preservation bylaw, its ambiguity, and how to simplify the application and review process. Members took homework on a flowchart and application form revisions, and discussed the Ritter building window dispute with the Select Board. The only formal vote heard was accepting prior minutes.

budget_items.topic: Town funds given to the commission
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the town gave the commission a sum and suggested using it for a handbook for residents of historic homes.
A member said the town appropriated money for window restoration, painting and gutter and roof repairs, and worried replacing all windows would exceed it.
Lockwood suggested CPA funding as a possible incentive for preservation; the town has not passed it.

decisions.decision: Action items: members to individually review and draft an applicant flowchart/decision tree and a revised application form, in different versions, for the next meeting.
Next meeting planned for March 7th, subject to confirming room availability with the clerk.
Chair to write to the Select Board on behalf of the commission that a new application must be submitted; members agreed without a vote.

what_happened.line: The commission decided without a vote to write to the Select Board that a new application must be submitted for the Ritter building windows.
The Ritter window denial stands; the discussion with the Select Board produced no vote to reconsider it.
Members were assigned to draft an applicant flowchart and a revised application form, in separate versions, for the next meeting.
A new member led a long discussion of the bylaw's origin and intent, its ambiguity, and ways to reduce the review burden.
The only formal vote was to accept the prior minutes; the next meeting is planned for March 7, pending room availability.

why_it_matters: Owners of historic homes may soon face a simpler application and review process, but the bylaw itself has not changed and nothing here alters what is required today.

The Ritter building windows are a town-owned project funded by an appropriation; a required new application could delay the work, and a member worried replacing all the windows would exceed the money appropriated.
watch_next: Next commission meeting, planned for March 7 pending room confirmation: draft flowcharts and revised application forms are due.
Whether the Select Board files a new application for the Ritter windows, as the chair's letter requests.
